deliberate.2026-09-19 semitexa-orm 3 -> 4: The semitexa.builtSqlFragment rule ships in this cut and found one call: CollectionQueryCompiler::applyCursor()'s whereRaw(), given implode(' OR ', $branches) — a keyset-pagination predicate assembled at runtime because the branch count depends on the sort spec. Every identifier goes through SqlIdentifier::quote() and every value is a bound '?', so it is safe in substance but not by CONSTRUCTION, which is what the rule checks. A dynamic OR-chain cannot be a literal, so nothing short of restructuring cursor pagination satisfies it — ORM work, not release work. Recorded here rather than baselined, for the same reason AcceptedViolations gives: the rule keeps firing and the gate keeps reporting it.
